Title: HTI5007 Radiation Biology — Chapter 4 Protein Names: Decoder & Mnemonics (source: RadBio_Revision_Notes.pdf, Ch 4 pp. 93–125 and Ch 8 summary pp. 288–291)

SECTION 1 — Decode the names (what biologists actually use). Rule of thumb: -ase = enzyme; kinase adds a phosphate, phosphatase removes one; "p" = protein; Cdc/RAD/wee = yeast mutant names; ATM/NBS/Rb = named after a human disease.
Table columns: Name | What it really means | Hook
- p53, p21, p27, p16 | "p" = protein, number = size in kDa | Big number = big boss (p53). Small numbers (16, 21, 27) are the little wedges (CKIs) that jam a CDK
- CDK | Cyclin-Dependent Kinase; numbers = order of discovery, not order in the cycle | That's why the cycle goes 4/6 → 2 → 2 → 1, not 1-2-3-4
- Cyclin | Named because its level cycles up and down | Letters D, E, A, B = discovery order too
- CKI, CAK | CDK Inhibitor; CDK-Activating Kinase | "CAK Can Activate Kinase"
- Cdc25, Cdc2 | Cell Division Cycle mutant no. 25 / no. 2 (yeast) | Cdc2 = CDK1 in old papers
- Wee1 | Yeast mutants lacking it divide too early → tiny "wee" cells | "Wee1 says Wait" (puts the tired-phosphate on Tyr)
- ATM / ATR | Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated / ATM-and-Rad3-Related | Named after the disease of patients who lack it
- CHK1, CHK2 | CHecKpoint Kinase | Two broken strands (DSB) → ATM → CHK2; one strand (replication stress) → ATR → CHK1
- MRN = MRE11 + RAD50 + NBS1 | Meiotic REcombination 11, RADiation-sensitive 50, Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome 1 | "Mr N" — the night-watchman who finds the break
- H2AX → γH2AX | Histone H2A variant X; γ = the phosphorylated form | γ-rays leave γ-flags (foci) at each break
- MDM2 | Mouse Double Minute 2 (a gene amplified in mouse cells) | "Marks p53 for DeMolition"
- CDKN1A (= p21) | CDK iNhibitor 1A | The gene name of the bouncer
- Rb | RetinoBlastoma (childhood eye tumour when it's lost) | "Road Block" / the brake
- E2F | adenovirus E2-promoter-binding Factor | "Entry-to-S Factor" — the ignition key Rb holds
- Bax | Bcl-2-Associated X protein | "p53 swings the axe" at the mitochondrion
- Caspase-3 | Cysteine-ASPartate protease | The executioner's cleaver
- Ubiquitin / proteasome | "ubiquitous" tag / protein-body shredder | Kiss-of-death tag → shredder
- Luciferase, GFP, Cas9, HSV1-tk, OTC | light-bearer (Lucifer) enzyme; Green Fluorescent Protein; CRISPR-ASsociated 9; Herpes simplex virus 1 thymidine kinase; Ornithine TransCarbamylase | All plain acronyms once expanded

SECTION 2 — Invented devices
A. Cyclin order through the cycle — "DEAB": Decide, Enter, Advance, Burst
- Cyclin D – CDK4/6: G1, the cell Decides to divide
- Cyclin E – CDK2: Enter S (G1/S border)
- Cyclin A – CDK2: Advance through S and into G2 (the 2024 Q35 answer: CDK2 at S/G2)
- Cyclin B – CDK1: Burst into mitosis (G2/M)
CDK partners: "4-6-2-2-1, like a countdown — the cycle counts down to 1 = mitosis (CDK1)." D takes the pair (4/6), E and A share 2, B gets 1.

B. The five switches on a CDK — "B-CAK, Wee, Cdc, CKI"
Bind cyclin (on) → CAK on Thr (on) → Wee1 on Tyr (off) → Cdc25 strips Tyr-phosphate (on again) → CKI p21/p27/p16 (off). Notes' own line (p. 101): Thr = thrive, Tyr = tired; add "Wee1 makes it Weary, Cdc25 is the Cure."

C. The SQ1 chain (DSB → G1 arrest) — story: "Mr N calls ATM, ATM checks (CHK2) and flags (γH2AX); p53 escapes the MDM2 bodyguard, hires the p21 bouncer, who blocks cyclin E–CDK2; Rb keeps the key (E2F); no entry to S."
Acronym for the order: M-A-C-P-P-C-R-E → "My ATM Card Pays Pocket Cash, Really Easy" = MRN, ATM, CHK2, p53, p21, CDK2 blocked, Rb, E2F.
Five mark-earning steps: Sense – Signal – Stabilise – Effector – Arrest (S-S-S-E-A), as in Problem 4.4: (1) MRN senses the DSB; (2) ATM phosphorylates CHK2, H2AX, p53; (3) p53 escapes MDM2 and builds up; (4) p53 switches on p21, p21 blocks cyclin E–CDK2 and cyclin D–CDK4/6; (5) Rb stays hypophosphorylated, holds E2F, cell stops at G1/S; outcome = repair / apoptosis / senescence.

D. The G2/M checkpoint (no p53) — "ATM/ATR → CHK1/2 ⊣ Cdc25 ⊣ CDK1": "Checks Cancel the Cure" (CHK cancels Cdc25, so CDK1 stays weary). Exam contrast: G1 arrest needs p53, G2 arrest does not — "G1 has 1 guardian; G2 goes without." (About half of human cancers have broken TP53.)

E. Checkpoint proteins (notes p. 96 table) — "G1 is a PERP" (p53, E2F, Rb, p21); "Intra-S has 2 A's and 2 C's" (ATM, ATR, CHK1, CHK2); "G2/M: CHK1 Cuts Cdc25, Cyclin B–CDK1."

F. Apoptosis route — "p53 → Bax → cyt c → caspase-3": "Bax Cracks the Cell" (Bax, Cytochrome c, Caspase).

G. CKIs p16, p21, p27 — "16-21-27: teenager, adult, late-twenties — all three refuse to let the CDK party start"; p21 is the one p53 orders (gene CDKN1A).

H. Blots — standard SNoW DRoP (Southern–DNA, Northern–RNA, Western–Protein). Add: "Southern is the only person (Edwin Southern, 1975); the others are compass jokes."

I. Gene delivery — "Trans-FORM-ation for bacteria (heat shock), trans-FECT-ion for eukaryote cells without virus (electroporation, sonoporation, calcium phosphate, Lipofectamine), trans-DUCT-ion needs a viral conDUCTor." (2024 Q2: heat-shock transformation cannot transfer genes into mammalian cells.)

J. Silencing (2024 Q29) — "si, sh, mi, CRISPR silence; mRNA is the Messenger — you don't silence a message by sending more of it." siRNA transient; shRNA stable via vector; miRNA natural, blocks translation; CRISPR/Cas9 cuts the gene, permanent knockout.

K. Vectors — "Lentivirus = Long-term, Lazy cells (integrates, infects non-dividing, ~9 kb); Adeno = Alarm (strong immune response, Jesse Gelsinger 1999); AAV = Almost no Alarm but small; HSV = Huge capacity."

SECTION 3 — How to make these stick
1. Draw the SQ1 chain from memory every day (blank page, 2 minutes), then compare with Fig 4.2 / p. 102. The 11-step list collapses to the 5-step S-S-S-E-A answer that earns the marks.
2. Use the "tag" trick when reading: every time a name appears, say its expansion out loud ("checkpoint kinase 2"). After three readings the expansion is the memory, not the letters.
3. Group by role, not alphabet — sensors (MRN), transducers (ATM/ATR, CHK1/2), effectors (p53, p21, Cdc25), targets (cyclin–CDK, Rb, E2F). This matches how examiners phrase SQ1.
4. Put the DEAB and 4-6-2-2-1 lines on the same card as the Q35 fact (CDK2 at S/G2) — that's the one MC question drawn from this list.

Also already in the notes (keep as "standard" mnemonics): "Pure As Gold" for purines (A, G); "Thr = thrive, Tyr = tired" (p. 101); SNoW DRoP (p. 117).
